questions.stem: Which of the following checks to see if the assessable record exists for the demand and creates an assessable record if none exists?
questions.explanation: The 'Validate Assessment Metrics for Demand' business rule checks whether an assessable record exists for the demand and creates one if none exists. This ensures that when a demand enters the screening state, the assessment framework has a proper assessable record linked to the demand for stakeholder evaluations. Auto Business Rules and Update Demand State serve different purposes.

questions.stem: Projects and which other artifact can be linked to either a program, a portfolio, both, or neither.
questions.explanation: Projects and Demands can be linked to either a program, a portfolio, both, or neither. Demands serve as the primary intake mechanism for potential projects and share the ability to be associated with programs and portfolios. Test Cases, Resources, and Stories do not have direct program/portfolio associations at the same level.

questions.stem: If Scenario Planning for PPM is installed, a portfolio manager can access the Portfolio Planning Workbench by navigating to which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A portfolio manager can access the Portfolio Planning Workbench by navigating via the Portfolio Planning related link on a portfolio record or through the Portfolio Planning Workbench module in the application navigator. The Project module and Program Workbench do not provide direct access to portfolio planning functionality.

questions.stem: When creating a resource plan within a demand, how are the default dates on a resource plan determined?

options.text: From demand start date and due date
Resource plan(s) cannot be created from demand

questions.explanation: When creating a resource plan within a demand, the default dates are determined from the demand start date and due date. The resource plan inherits these dates to align resource allocation with the demand timeline. Resource plans can be created from demands, and portfolio dates or demand created dates are not used for this purpose.

questions.stem: A customer requires five (5) teamspaces to support different departments. What should you do?

options.text: Contact the Account Representative to activate the teamspaces.
Use UI Policies and Business Rules to enable teamspaces.

questions.explanation: To activate five teamspaces for different departments, you should contact the Account Representative to activate the teamspaces. Teamspaces require entitlement activation through ServiceNow — they cannot be self-activated via properties, plugins, or custom configuration. Each teamspace provides isolated project management environments for different departments.

questions.stem: When setting-up a program, planned ROI% is calculated based on: (Choose two.)

options.text: Values in the Planned cost field.
Values in the Planned return field.
Values in the Budgeted cost field.

questions.explanation: Planned ROI% is calculated based on values in the Planned cost field and the Planned return field. The formula is: Planned ROI% = (Planned Return - Planned Cost) / Planned Cost × 100. NPV and Budgeted cost are separate financial metrics not directly used in the planned ROI percentage calculation.

questions.stem: Which plugin provides a layer of artificial intelligence that empowers features and capabilities across applications to provide better work experiences?
questions.explanation: Predictive Intelligence for PPM [com.snc.ppm_ml] provides a layer of artificial intelligence that empowers features and capabilities across applications to provide better work experiences. This plugin enables machine learning-powered predictions for project and demand management. Strategic Spend Tracking, Scenario Planning, and PPM Standard serve different purposes.

questions.stem: To use the Time Sheet dashboard, what plugin must be installed?

options.text: Common ITSM Service Portal Application Components (com.snc.app_common.service_portal)
Performance Analytics – Content Pack – PPM Standard plugin (com.snc.pa.pmo_dashboards)

questions.explanation: The Performance Analytics Content Pack for PPM Standard plugin (com.snc.pa.pmo_dashboards) must be installed to use the Time Sheet dashboard. This plugin provides pre-built PA dashboards including the Time Sheet dashboard for tracking time card data. The other plugins serve different purposes unrelated to time sheet reporting.

questions.stem: Where do you define ‘Roles’ requested via resource plans?

options.text: No need to define it differently, they are same are system roles

questions.explanation: Resource roles requested via resource plans are defined under Resource Roles in the Resource Management module. These are distinct from system security roles — they represent project resource types like Developer, Business Analyst, or Architect. They are configured specifically for resource planning purposes and determine rate cards and skill requirements.

questions.stem: Plugins may be added to the base platform in one of the following ways: (Choose three.)

options.text: Activated by an admin (not by default).
Activated by default in the base ServiceNow system.

questions.explanation: Plugins can be added to the base platform in three ways: Activated by an admin (not by default) for plugins available in the instance but not pre-activated, Requested from ServiceNow for plugins requiring ServiceNow enablement, and Activated by default in the base ServiceNow system for plugins that come pre-installed. The it_portfolio_manager and it_pps_admin roles cannot activate plugins.

questions.stem: What does the project status report allow project managers to do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Show historical trend of project KPI’s

questions.explanation: The project status report allows project managers to Show historical trend of project KPIs (tracking health over time) and Print as a PDF attachment (for sharing with stakeholders). The Gantt chart is viewed on the Planning Console, and WBS is viewed in the project structure — neither are status report features.

questions.stem: How does a project manager request a change to a resource plan in the requested state?
questions.explanation: A project manager requests a change to a resource plan in the requested state by using the 'Request change on resource plan' action. This creates a formal change request for the resource manager to review and approve. Using notes, emailing the resource user, or emailing the resource manager are informal methods not built into the process flow.

questions.stem: In which table can you find cost information for a specific fiscal period?
questions.explanation: The cost_plan_breakdown table stores cost information for specific fiscal periods. Cost plan breakdowns contain the period-by-period financial data (planned, actual, forecast costs) aligned to fiscal periods. The cost_plan table stores the overall plan, expense_line stores individual expenses, and pm_project is the project table.

questions.stem: What is the default schedule for a project?
questions.explanation: The default schedule for a project is an 8-hour workday from 8:00 to 12:00 and 1:00 to 5:00 (with a 1-hour lunch break). This is the standard PPM default schedule that repeats weekly on weekdays Monday through Friday. Other options represent incorrect time ranges.

questions.stem: The PPM Standard plugin enables an it_project_manager to perform the following activities: (Choose three.)

options.text: Establish resource requirements and track costs.
Track actual amount spent compared to an approved budget.

questions.explanation: The PPM Standard plugin enables an it_project_manager to: Determine overall project cost requirements (A) through cost planning, Establish resource requirements and track costs (D) via resource plans, and Track actual amount spent compared to an approved budget (E) through financial tracking. Configuring cost type definitions and defining portfolio targets require admin or portfolio manager roles.

questions.stem: When a time card is approved, the actual time is stored in which two tables? (Choose two.)

options.text: Resource Aggregate tables (Daily, Weekly, and Monthly)

questions.explanation: When a time card is approved, the actual time is stored in the Project Time table (records individual time entries against tasks) and the Resource Aggregate tables (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) which aggregate time data for reporting and utilization calculations. The Resource Allocation Daily table stores planned allocations, and Resource Event stores resource events.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles can access the project administration application?
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin role can access the Project Administration application. This administrative role manages PPM configuration including project settings, preferences, and administration modules. The it_project_user, it_project_manager, and timecard_admin roles have access to their respective functional areas but not the administration application.

questions.stem: The Project Portfolio Management application supports domain separation at this level:
questions.explanation: The Project Portfolio Management application supports domain separation at Level 2 — Tenant process management. This level allows each tenant to manage their own processes, workflows, and configurations while sharing the underlying platform. Level 3 (self-managed configuration) and Level 1 (data only) are different separation levels.

questions.stem: The hourly rate is derived from the resource rate on the resource plan, if this option is selected.
questions.explanation: The hourly rate is derived from the resource rate on the resource plan when the Rate model option is selected. Rate models provide date-effective, criteria-driven hourly rates for resource cost calculations. Rate override allows manual specification, Labor rate card uses predefined rates, and Planned cost is an output, not an input option.

questions.stem: Which role can configure the parameters of the demand workbench that is provided with the base system?
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin role can configure the parameters of the demand workbench provided with the base system. This role has administrative access to PPM configuration including workbench settings under Workbench Config - Demand. Project managers, business stakeholders, and other roles lack the configuration privileges for the demand workbench.

questions.stem: Depending on the execution type selected for a particular project, one of these dashboards will also be available:
questions.explanation: Depending on the execution type selected for a project, the Project Summary — Waterfall Dashboard will also be available. When a project uses the Waterfall execution type, this dashboard provides waterfall-specific views including Gantt charts, milestones, and phase tracking. The Timecard and PMO dashboards are separate, and User Manager Dashboard is not a standard PPM dashboard.

questions.stem: In order to submit an idea, what application would a user access?
questions.explanation: To submit an idea, a user accesses the Idea Portal. The Idea Portal provides a user-friendly interface for submitting, viewing, and voting on ideas. It is separate from Demand, Project, and Change applications — ideas go through their own lifecycle before potentially being converted to demands or projects.

questions.stem: Which ‘Member Preference’ automatically finds the most available resource(s) from the group and allocates to a plan using the allocation action?
questions.explanation: The 'Any member' preference automatically finds the most available resource(s) from the group and allocates to a plan using the allocation action. When set to Any member, the system evaluates group members' availability and selects the most available resource. All members selects everyone, and Specific member requires manual selection.

questions.stem: An it_pps_admin user is able to update: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An it_pps_admin user is able to update Budget Periods (managing fiscal period definitions) and Portfolio Targets (setting CAPEX/OPEX targets for portfolios). Client Scripts and Business Rules are platform configuration items that require the admin or developer role, not the it_pps_admin role.

questions.stem: What role can configure an idea module, map idea categories to the idea module, and add navigation for the Idea Portal?
questions.explanation: The idea_admin role can configure an idea module, map idea categories to the idea module, and add navigation for the Idea Portal. This role provides full administrative control over the ideation framework. Project managers manage projects, idea managers manage idea lifecycle, and demand managers handle demands — none have idea module configuration access.

questions.stem: Which roles can view reports on resource utilization and availability? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The it_project_portfolio_user and resource_manager roles can view reports on resource utilization and availability. Portfolio users need visibility into resource usage across the portfolio, while resource managers need to monitor their resources' allocation and availability. The pps_resource role provides basic resource access, and resource_user is for individual resource functions.

questions.stem: What role can create or modify a rate model?
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin role can create or modify a rate model. Rate models define date-effective, criteria-driven hourly rates for resource cost calculations and are a PPM administrative configuration. The time_card_admin, push_admin, and release_admin roles serve different functions and do not have rate model management access.

questions.stem: To set up a group for selection in a resource plan, the group record needs to include which role?
questions.explanation: To set up a group for selection in a resource plan, the group record needs to include the pps_resource role. This role identifies users and groups as available resources for project planning purposes. Without this role, the group will not appear as a selectable option in resource plans. The itil, it_project_user, and resource_manager roles serve different purposes.

questions.stem: When can a user choose from multiple rate types for their work, while logging a time card?

options.text: Only if the capability is enabled in the Project Preferences
Only if this capability is enabled in the Project Record
Only one (1) rate type can apply
Only if the capability is enabled in the Time Sheet Policies

questions.explanation: A user can choose from multiple rate types for their work while logging a time card only if this capability is enabled in the Time Sheet Policies. Time Sheet Policies control the rules and options available during time entry, including whether multiple rate types are available. Project Preferences and Project Records do not control this specific capability.

questions.stem: What is the difference between confirm and allocate actions?

options.text: Confirm action creates hard allocation and allocate action creates soft allocation.
Confirm action creates soft allocation and allocate action creates hard allocation.
Allocate action is always followed by confirm action.

questions.explanation: The confirm action creates soft allocation (tentative booking) and the allocate action creates hard allocation (committed booking). Soft allocations from confirm indicate planned resource usage, while hard allocations from allocate represent committed resource assignments that affect capacity calculations. They do not function the same way and are not sequential.

questions.stem: If a user creates a new demand from the demand workbench, what state will the system save the record in?
questions.explanation: If a user creates a new demand from the demand workbench, the system saves the record in draft state. Draft is the initial state for demands, allowing the creator to add details before submitting. The demand must progress through the lifecycle (draft → submitted → screening → qualified → approved) before it reaches later states.

questions.stem: In order for a business unit to have its own Idea Portal to retrieve data, what must be configured first?

options.text: A business unit cannot have its own its own Idea Portal

questions.explanation: For a business unit to have its own Idea Portal to retrieve data, an Idea module must be configured first. Each business unit needs its own idea module (with a unique Module ID used as a URL parameter) to direct users to the correct portal instance. Idea categories and portal URLs are configured within the module. A business unit can have its own portal.

questions.stem: What needs to be configured if a customer wants to change the attributes copied when using copy project or copy partial project?
questions.explanation: To change the attributes copied when using copy project or copy partial project, the com.snc.project.copy.additional_attributes property must be configured. This property specifies which additional fields beyond the defaults are included in the copy operation. The copy project client script, UI action, and com.snc.project.copy are not the correct configuration points.

questions.stem: When entering time worked into a time sheet, which feature is recommended to group different types of work (e.g., standard hours and overtime)?
questions.explanation: Rate type is the recommended feature to group different types of work such as standard hours and overtime when entering time on a time sheet. Rate types categorize time entries by work type, enabling different billing rates and reporting for various work categories. Bill rate is a monetary value, Category serves a different purpose, and Rate model defines cost calculation rules.

questions.stem: What system role is needed to manage programs?
questions.explanation: The it_program_manager role is the system role needed to manage programs. This role provides access to create, edit, and manage program records, associated projects, and program tasks. The it_project_manager manages projects, it_portfolio_manager_admin is not a standard role, and it_program_manager_admin is not the correct role name.

questions.stem: Who can submit Ideas?
questions.explanation: Any user can submit Ideas through the Idea Portal. The ideation process is designed to be inclusive — anyone in the organization can contribute ideas regardless of their role. This broad access ensures that good ideas from all levels of the organization can be captured. Ideas do not require IT, demand, or ITIL roles to submit.

questions.stem: Where can a user export project data in either a MPP, XML or CSV format?
questions.explanation: A user can export project data in MPP, XML, or CSV format from the Planning Console. The Planning Console provides the project structure view with export capabilities to these formats for integration with tools like Microsoft Project. The Demand Form, Related lists, and Project Workbench do not offer these export format options.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true regarding how the My Project Space (Project Workspace) handles dynamic content? (Choose two.)

options.text: If the project state is On Hold, actual start date and actual end date are displayed.
If the project state is Pending or Open, planned start date and planned end date are displayed.
If the project state is Draft, actual start date and actual end date are displayed.
If the project state is Work in Progress, actual start date and planned end date are displayed.

questions.explanation: In My Project Space (Project Workspace): If the project state is Pending or Open, planned start date and planned end date are displayed (since work hasn't begun), and if the project state is Work in Progress, actual start date and planned end date are displayed (work has started but not finished). On Hold shows actual start and planned end, and Draft typically shows planned dates.

questions.stem: Which of the following states appear in the process flow indicator at the top of the Demand form by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The default Demand form process flow indicator shows Draft (initial state), Approved (final approval state), and Screening (evaluation state where assessments are triggered). The full default flow is: Draft → Submitted → Screening → Qualified → Approved. Updated and Deferred are not part of the default process flow indicator.

questions.stem: Where are CAPEX and OPEX targets set for each fiscal year?
questions.explanation: CAPEX and OPEX targets for each fiscal year are set in the Portfolio Target. Portfolio targets define the financial boundaries (capital expenditure and operating expenditure) that portfolio managers use to evaluate and prioritize demands and projects. The Demand Workbench, Cost Plans, and Program Workbench are not where these targets are configured.

questions.stem: Which plugin activates the ideas module to gather and evaluate ideas efficiently, and quickly identify ideas for implementation?
questions.explanation: The Ideation with PPM plugin activates the ideas module to gather and evaluate ideas efficiently and quickly identify ideas for implementation. This plugin provides the Idea Portal, idea modules, idea categories, and the idea lifecycle management framework. Resource Management, Test Management, and Agile Development serve different purposes.

questions.stem: In what way would you restrict the assigned to field on a project task to only allow users with resource allocations to be assigned?

options.text: Create an Access Control List (ACL) rule.
On the project record under the preferences tab select the “Derive assignee list from resource plan” preference.
The system automatically does this and can only be disabled by an admin.
Create a reference qualifier on the ‘assigned to’ field.

questions.explanation: To restrict the assigned to field on a project task to only allow users with resource allocations, select the 'Derive assignee list from resource plan' preference on the project record under the Preferences tab. This ensures only resources with active allocations can be assigned to tasks, maintaining alignment between resource plans and task assignments.

questions.stem: At a minimum, which role is required to view the summary of a project in the Details tab of Project Workspace?
questions.explanation: At minimum, the it_project_user role is required to view the summary of a project in the Details tab of Project Workspace. This role provides read access to project information. The it_project_manager and it_portfolio_manager roles have broader access, and itil alone does not grant PPM project viewing access.

questions.stem: What is the demand workbench used for? (Choose two.)

options.text: Comparing and prioritizing demands against other demands.

questions.explanation: The demand workbench is used for displaying submitted demands to stakeholders (providing visibility into the demand pipeline) and comparing and prioritizing demands against other demands (enabling evaluation and ranking). The workbench does not directly approve demands or compare demands with portfolios — those are separate functions.

questions.stem: What applications are shared across teamspaces?
questions.explanation: Project Financials, Agile, and Test applications are shared across teamspaces. These applications operate at the platform level rather than being isolated within individual teamspaces. Resource management is also shared, but the specific combination asked here is Project Financials, Agile, and Test as the shared applications.

questions.stem: A project expense line is a cost associated with a specific source. Examples of specific sources could include: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Project expense line sources include User (labor costs from time entries), Configuration Item (CI-associated costs), and Fixed Asset (capital asset costs). These represent the specific sources that generate expense lines. Demand and Project are the entities that contain expense lines, not sources themselves.

questions.stem: Which roles can modify agile properties? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin and admin roles can modify agile properties. Agile properties are system-level configuration settings that require administrative access. Product owners and scrum masters work within the agile framework but cannot modify the underlying system properties that govern agile behavior.

questions.stem: In the base system, what is the default number of cards that can be displayed in the project workspace?
questions.explanation: The default number of cards that can be displayed in the project workspace is 1500 in the base system. This limit controls how many project cards are rendered in the My Projects Space page. This value can be configured by administrators if needed. Values of 10, 200, or 1 are not the default.

questions.stem: Demand managers can enhance a demand request by adding the following: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Demand managers can enhance a demand request by adding Requirements (defining what the demand needs), Decisions (recording key decisions made about the demand), and Stakeholders (identifying involved parties). These are available as related lists on the demand form. Change Requests and Problems are ITSM artifacts, not demand enhancements.

questions.stem: This should be updated by an it_pps_admin, so that the stakeholder list will automatically populate when a user creates a demand or project.
questions.explanation: The Stakeholder registry should be updated by an it_pps_admin so that the stakeholder list automatically populates when a user creates a demand or project. The stakeholder registry maps users to portfolios, and when a demand or project is associated with a portfolio, the registered stakeholders are automatically added. The Application registry serves a different purpose.

questions.stem: What happens to the expense line after it is processed?

options.text: The actual cost is recorded at the portfolio level.
The actual amount incurred becomes part of the cost plan.

questions.explanation: After an expense line is processed, the actual amount incurred becomes part of the cost plan. Expense lines feed their actual costs into the associated cost plan breakdowns, updating the actual cost figures. This allows project managers to track actual spending against planned budgets. The cost plan does not close, and costs are tracked at the project level, not portfolio level.

questions.stem: A pps_admin role can configure the parameters that are displayed on a project card. The parameters displayed on a project card are derived from the records in what table?
questions.explanation: The parameters displayed on a project card are derived from records in the PM Home Page Card [pm_home_page_card] table. This table defines which fields and information appear on project cards in the Project Workspace. The it_pps_admin role configures these cards. The other tables serve entirely different purposes.

questions.stem: What creates calendar entries on a user’s individual calendar? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Allocated resource plans and Confirmed resource plans create calendar entries on a user's individual calendar. Allocated plans (hard allocations) and confirmed plans (soft allocations) both generate calendar bookings showing the resource's committed and tentative assignments. Approved and Planned states do not generate calendar entries — the resource must be allocated or confirmed first.

questions.stem: If the Agile Development 2.0 plugin is activated, an idea can be converted into which of the following task types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: With Agile Development 2.0 activated, an idea can be converted into a Story (user story for agile backlog), an Epic (large body of work), or a Project (traditional project execution). These conversion options allow ideas to be implemented through different execution methods. SAFe features and SAFe epics require additional SAFe plugin activation.

questions.stem: The RIDAC workflow can be modified by using which feature?
questions.explanation: The RIDAC (Risks, Issues, Decisions, Actions, Changes) workflow can be modified using Flow Designer. Flow Designer is the recommended modern automation tool for customizing workflows in ServiceNow, including RIDAC processes. The Project Form and Service Catalog are not workflow modification tools, and the Idea Portal is for submitting ideas.

questions.stem: An it_project_manager can request resources by which of the following: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: An it_project_manager can request resources by Hours and Person Days. These are two of the three effort types available for resource planning (the third being FTE). When creating a resource plan request, the project manager specifies the effort in hours or person days. Month and Day are not valid request types.

questions.stem: Which of these tools allow you pinpoint over-allocated resources by viewing their negative availability values? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Resource Allocation Workbench and Resource Reports allow you to pinpoint over-allocated resources by viewing their negative availability values. The Resource Allocation Workbench shows real-time allocation vs capacity, and Resource Reports provide detailed utilization analysis. The Project Workbench and Resource Plan Logs do not specifically show negative availability values.

questions.stem: How is a resource group’s capacity derived for resource planning?

options.text: Aggregate capacity of all its members.

questions.explanation: A resource group's capacity is derived from the aggregate capacity of all its members. The system calculates the group's total capacity by summing the individual capacities of each group member based on their schedules and FTE values. Capacity is not stored in a single table field or group record — it is dynamically calculated from members.

questions.stem: The information displayed on Project Workspace is setup in which table?
questions.explanation: The information displayed on Project Workspace is set up in the pm_home_page_card table. This table contains the configuration records that define which parameters, fields, and data appear on project cards and workspace sections. The vtb_card and vtb_card_history are Visual Task Board tables, and pm_project is the project table itself.

questions.stem: Which capability allows users to view variances in a project’s schedule?
questions.explanation: Compare scheduled baselines allows users to view variances in a project's schedule. By comparing the current project schedule against saved baselines, managers can identify schedule slippage, date changes, and other variances. Move project changes dates, Project Status Report shows current status, and machine-learning algorithms predict outcomes rather than show schedule variances.

questions.stem: What role can configure the default columns in the project planning console? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The admin and it_pps_admin roles can configure the default columns in the project planning console. These administrative roles have access to the planning console configuration settings. The it_project_manager uses the console but cannot configure its default columns, and it_console_admin is not a standard PPM role.

questions.stem: Which table stores daily capacity of a user?
questions.explanation: The Resource_Aggregate_Daily table stores the daily capacity of a user. This table contains aggregated resource data including available capacity, allocated hours, and confirmed hours on a daily basis. Resource_Allocation_Daily stores allocation data, Resource_Event stores task time blocks, and User Profile stores user information but not daily capacity.

questions.stem: Users with what role can be considered for resource planning?
questions.explanation: Users with the pps_resource role can be considered for resource planning. This role marks a user as an available resource in the PPM resource pool. Without this role, users will not appear in resource plan selection lists. The it_user, it_project_user, and it_pps_user roles serve different functions and do not make users available for resource planning.

questions.stem: What features are not included in a teamspace application but can be added in teamspace settings? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Idea and Demand Assessments are not included in a teamspace application by default but can be added through teamspace settings. The core teamspace includes project management features, but ideation and demand assessment capabilities are optional additions. Workbench configuration and Project are included in the base teamspace application.

questions.stem: Is resource capacity derived from FTE or schedules?
questions.explanation: Resource capacity is derived from Both FTE and schedules. The system uses the user's FTE value (Full-Time Equivalent) multiplied by their assigned schedule to calculate their available capacity. For example, a user with 1.0 FTE and an 8-hour weekday schedule has 8 hours of daily capacity. Neither alone determines capacity.

questions.stem: How is the Resource Management application activated?

options.text: Installed as part of Release Management plugin
Installed as part of adding users
Installed automatically as part of new system

questions.explanation: The Resource Management application is installed with the PPM Standard plugin. When PPM Standard (com.snc.financial_planning_pmo) is activated, Resource Management is included as part of the installation. It is not part of Release Management, user provisioning, or automatic system installation.

questions.stem: Can an it_project_manager convert a task to a milestone?

options.text: Yes, it must be manually done from the project record.
Yes, from the planning console right-click a task and select convert to milestone.
No, the task must be deleted and re-created.
No, this can only be done by an admin.

questions.explanation: Yes, an it_project_manager can convert a task to a milestone by right-clicking a task in the planning console and selecting 'Convert to Milestone.' This action changes the task to a zero-duration milestone marker. It does not require manual changes on the project record, deletion, or admin privileges.

questions.stem: Which field on the Idea Module form displays the unique identifier for the module, that is used as a parameter in the Idea Portal URL to direct users?
questions.explanation: The Module ID field on the Idea Module form displays the unique identifier used as a parameter in the Idea Portal URL to direct users to the correct portal instance. Each business unit's Idea Portal uses this Module ID (sysparm_module_id) in the URL to retrieve the appropriate ideas and categories for that unit.

questions.stem: Which users have access the project administration application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin and admin roles have access to the project administration application. These administrative roles can access Project Administration modules including settings, preferences, and configuration. The it_portfolio_manager and it_project_manager roles access their respective functional areas but not the administration application.

questions.stem: The Business Unit field on a Project or displays values from a specific table. What type of field is this?
questions.explanation: The Business Unit field on a Project displays values from a specific table and is a Reference field type. Reference fields in ServiceNow point to records in another table (in this case, the business_unit table) and display a selection from that table. Conditions, Journal, and List are different field types.

questions.stem: If an it_project_manager does not want to equally distribute hours across the resource plan time frame, what allocation spread should be used?
questions.explanation: If an it_project_manager does not want to equally distribute hours across the resource plan time frame, the Front Load allocation spread should be used. Front Load distributes more hours at the beginning of the time frame, gradually decreasing. Back Load does the opposite (more hours at the end), Even distributes equally, and Any is not a valid spread type.

questions.stem: Using the Request type field on a resource plan, which options can be used to request a resource? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Using the Request type field on a resource plan, resources can be requested by Hours (specific hour count), FTE (Full-Time Equivalent fraction), and Person Days (number of work days). These are the three effort types available for resource planning. Month and Day are time periods, not request types.

questions.stem: What are the possible breakdown types of a cost plan breakdown? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The possible breakdown types of a cost plan breakdown are: Requirement (cost by requirement), Project (project-level costs), Task (task-level costs), and Portfolio (portfolio-level costs). These four types allow cost tracking at different hierarchy levels. Demand costs are tracked separately before conversion to projects, and Program and other types exist but the four main breakdown types are these.

questions.stem: Where is planned cost calculated from when requesting resources from a group and when resource role is specified?

options.text: The hourly rate of the specified role.

questions.explanation: When requesting resources from a group with a specified resource role, the planned cost is calculated from the hourly rate of the specified role. Resource roles have associated rates that determine the cost of allocation. The hourly rate on the role record is used as the basis for planned cost calculation, not task rate cards, distribution costs, or CI rate cards.

questions.stem: What is a Program?

options.text: A group of related projects and program activities.
A group of related projects, ideas, demands, and task activities.
A group of related projects, demands, and program activities.

questions.explanation: A Program is a group of related projects and program activities. Programs serve as containers for managing multiple related projects that together achieve a strategic objective. Program activities include program-specific tasks, risks, issues, and decisions. Programs do not directly contain ideas or demands — those exist at the portfolio and demand management level.

questions.stem: If you want the project planned start date to remain the same despite the start date of the earliest task, what property would you disable?

options.text: Roll up project start date from tasks [com.snc.project.rollup_project_start_date].
Max date span into future or past from the current date for the project/project task [com.snc.project.task.check_date_span_years].
Retain start on constraint on tasks after adding relations [com.snc.project.allow_start_on_relations].
Max duration allowed for a project/project task [com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration].

questions.explanation: To keep the project planned start date the same regardless of the earliest task start date, disable the property 'Roll up project start date from tasks' (com.snc.project.rollup_project_start_date). When enabled, this property automatically adjusts the project start date to match the earliest task. Disabling it preserves the manually set project start date.

questions.stem: Which is the minimum role that has access to the Project Administration > Settings > Preferences-Project module?
questions.explanation: The minimum role with access to the Project Administration > Settings > Preferences-Project module is it_pps_admin. This role manages PPM configuration and preferences. While sys_admin also has access, it_pps_admin is the minimum required role. it_project_manager and it_program_manager access project and program management but not administration settings.

questions.stem: When creating a project from demand, what related records are moved and copied upon Project Creation?
questions.explanation: When creating a project from demand, the Resource Plan and Cost Plan related records are moved and copied upon project creation. These financial and resource planning artifacts transfer from the demand to the new project to maintain continuity. Change Requests, Assessments, Ideas, and the Demand record itself remain associated with the demand.

questions.stem: How many WBS levels can be shown on the planning console?
questions.explanation: There is No Limit to the number of WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) levels that can be shown on the planning console. Projects can have deeply nested parent-child task hierarchies with unlimited levels. The planning console displays all levels of the task structure regardless of depth.

questions.stem: What is a data copy of the current project’s task, schedule, or structure that can be used for comparison reporting later?
questions.explanation: A Baseline is a data copy of the current project's task, schedule, or structure that can be used for comparison reporting later. Creating a baseline captures a snapshot of the project plan at a point in time. Multiple baselines can be saved and compared against the current schedule to identify variances. Accruals, Forecasts, and Commitments serve different financial purposes.

questions.stem: A checklist item record provides a name and what other element?
questions.explanation: A checklist item record provides a name and a Complete field. The Complete field is a boolean (true/false) that indicates whether the checklist item has been finished. Checklist items are simple completion tracking records without status fields, percent complete, or short descriptions — just a name and a completion flag.

questions.stem: The project property to update actual effort from time card is controlled at what level?
questions.explanation: The project property to update actual effort from time card is controlled at the Project Level. This setting is configured on individual project records under the Preferences tab, allowing different projects to handle time card actuals differently. It is not a global, program, or portfolio level setting.

questions.stem: What is a resource event?

options.text: An event scheduled by a project manager.
A block of time that a resource spends on a task.

questions.explanation: A resource event is a block of time that a resource spends on a task. Resource events are created when resources are allocated to tasks and represent the specific time periods during which work is performed. They are stored in the resource_event table and track the effort against each task assignment.

questions.stem: What happens to resource allocations with actual hours after a resource plan is cancelled?

options.text: The allocated hours remain until the project is closed.
The allocated hours become zero and the actual hours are retained.
A resource plan with actual hours cannot be canceled.
They are automatically moved to the next resource plan in the project.

questions.explanation: When a resource plan with actual hours is cancelled, the allocated hours become zero and the actual hours are retained. The system preserves the record of work already done (actual hours) but removes future allocations (allocated hours become zero). This ensures historical time data is not lost while freeing future capacity.

questions.stem: A program is a container for the following except for:
questions.explanation: A program is a container for program tasks, issues, and cost plans, but NOT for Portfolios. Portfolios are higher-level containers that hold programs and projects, not the other way around. A program sits within a portfolio hierarchy — it does not contain portfolios. Programs manage related projects and program-specific activities.

questions.stem: Which related lists should primarily be used to capture financial data in a project? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Cost Plans and Monetary Benefit Plans are the primary related lists for capturing financial data in a project. Cost Plans track planned, actual, and forecast costs, while Monetary Benefit Plans capture expected financial returns. Risks track potential issues, and Programs are organizational containers — neither primarily captures financial data.

questions.stem: Use this table to configure the parameters displayed on a project card on the My Projects Space page of the Project Workspace.
questions.explanation: The pm_home_page_config table is used to configure the parameters displayed on a project card on the My Projects Space page of the Project Workspace. This table contains the configuration settings that control card appearance and content. The pm_project stores projects, project_template_config stores template settings, and pm_toplevel_project tracks top-level projects.

questions.stem: Which statement defines the Project Workspace?

options.text: A central location to view of all projects in a portfolio to prioritize work
A central location for creating and managing projects
A central location for viewing and assessing business demands
A central location transform the navigation of lists and forms into an interactive graphical experience

questions.explanation: Project Workspace is a central location for creating and managing projects. It provides project managers and team members with a unified interface to view project cards, access project details, manage tasks, and track progress. It is not for viewing portfolios, assessing demands, or navigating lists/forms — those are other workbenches and tools.

questions.stem: A user’s availability is calculated as:

options.text: Allocated hours divided by the total capacity
Sum of allocated and confirmed hours, divided by the total capacity

questions.explanation: A user's availability is calculated as Capacity minus allocation. Availability represents how many hours a resource has remaining after subtracting their current allocations from their total capacity. Allocated time alone is the booking, not availability. Utilization ratios (allocated/capacity or (allocated+confirmed)/capacity) measure usage, not availability.

questions.stem: A project expense line is cost associated with a specific source, except for:
questions.explanation: A project expense line is a cost associated with a specific source, except for Program. Valid expense line sources include resources, fixed assets, software, configuration items, and users. Programs are organizational containers that aggregate project costs but are not themselves sources of expense lines.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used to calculate planned cost when creating a resource plan? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When creating a resource plan, planned cost can be calculated using the Default rate (standard hourly rate for the resource) or a Rate card (predefined rate tables). These two options provide the cost basis for resource plan financial calculations. Demand rate and Project rate are not valid cost calculation options for resource plans.

questions.stem: If a project manager is responsible for approving time sheets or submitting time cards on behalf of team members, they should be given what role?
questions.explanation: If a project manager is responsible for approving time sheets or submitting time cards on behalf of team members, they should be given the timecard_admin role. This role provides administrative access to time card management including approval and proxy submission. The form_admin, approval_admin, and activity_admin roles serve different functions.

questions.stem: Which property controls the changes in cost and resource plans with respect to the change in the start date of a demand or project?

options.text: ‘Change Resource Plan, Cost Plan and Benefit Plan Start Date with Demand or Project Start Date Change’.
‘Enable altering of planned date for task in WIP/Closed’.
‘Calculate ROI percentage based on a project’s estimated cost and its net value’.

questions.explanation: The property 'Change Resource Plan, Cost Plan and Benefit Plan Start Date with Demand or Project Start Date Change' controls how cost and resource plans react to changes in the demand or project start date. When enabled, updating a demand or project start date automatically adjusts the associated resource plans, cost plans, and benefit plans.

questions.stem: If the ‘Move project for WIP projects’ property is enabled, project tasks associated with the project are also moved, except for tasks in which of the following states? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When 'Move project for WIP projects' is enabled, tasks in Closed and Work in Progress states are not moved. Tasks that are already completed (Closed) or actively being worked (Work in Progress) have their dates preserved since changing them would be disruptive. Tasks in Pending and Open states are moved as they haven't started yet.

questions.stem: Expenses and costs for a particular demand should be estimated before screening. When preparing the financials of a demand, what determines the present value of future cash flows?
questions.explanation: The Discount Rate % determines the present value of future cash flows when preparing demand financials. The discount rate is applied to future financial returns to calculate their present-day value (Net Present Value). A higher discount rate decreases the present value of future returns. Financial Return, Planned ROI, and Internal Rate of Return are outputs, not inputs to present value calculations.

questions.stem: Idea [im_idea_core] is directly extended from which table?

options.text: It is not extended from any table.

questions.explanation: The Idea [im_idea_core] table is directly extended from the Task table. Like many ServiceNow records (incidents, projects, changes), ideas inherit from the base task table, gaining standard fields like number, state, assigned to, and short description. It is not extended from Project, Idea Modules, or standalone.

questions.stem: The Defect and Enhancement type choices on a demand form are available only when which plugin is installed?
questions.explanation: The Defect and Enhancement type choices on a demand form are available only when the Agile Development 2.0 plugin is installed. This plugin adds agile-specific demand types, allowing demands to be converted into defects or enhancements. Without it, only standard demand types (Project, Change) are available. Ideation, Test Management, and Investment Funding plugins do not add these types.

questions.stem: The color band at the top of the project card in Project Workspace displays what project attribute?
questions.explanation: The color band at the top of the project card in Project Workspace displays the project's Status attribute (typically Health status — Green, Yellow, Red). This visual indicator gives managers a quick view of project health. Issues, Risk, and State are separate attributes not represented by the card's color band.

questions.stem: As an administrator, what can you use to customize the PPM Mobile application?
questions.explanation: Mobile Studio is the ServiceNow tool administrators use to customize the PPM Mobile application. It provides a drag-and-drop interface for configuring mobile app layouts, screens, and navigation without code. Self-Service is a portal framework, ATF Suites are for automated testing, and Service Catalog is for request management. None of those are designed for customizing mobile application layouts. Mobile Studio is specifically built for mobile app configuration and customization.

questions.stem: Demand assessments are triggered as soon as the demand enters what state?
questions.explanation: Demand assessments are triggered as soon as the demand enters the Screening state. In the demand lifecycle (Draft > Submitted > Screening > Qualified > Approved), assessments run during Screening to evaluate and score the demand before it advances. This allows stakeholders to review and rate demands as part of the qualification process. Assessments do not trigger at Submitted (too early, just received), Approved (too late, already accepted), or Qualified (assessments should already be complete by then).

questions.stem: Which demand category would a demand manager select, if they need to create an enhancement?
questions.explanation: A demand manager would select the Operational category to create an enhancement. The Operational demand category allows for enhancements and defects (when Agile Development 2.0 is active). The Strategic category is for strategic initiatives, Change is for change requests, and Defect is a type within a category, not a category itself.

questions.stem: On the demand form, what does the Discount Rate impact?
questions.explanation: The Discount Rate on the demand form impacts the Net Present Value (NPV). The discount rate is used to calculate the present value of projected future cash flows, which determines the NPV. A higher discount rate reduces the NPV. Internal Rate of Return is the rate at which NPV equals zero, ROI uses cost/return ratios, and Financial Benefit is an input.

questions.stem: As a demand manager, you can view an artifact from a demand. What artifacts are part of a demand?
questions.explanation: Artifacts that are part of a demand include Decision, Risk, and Requirements. These are available as related lists on the demand form through RIDAC (Risks, Issues, Decisions, Actions, Changes). Incidents, Problems, and Changes are ITSM artifacts. Stories, Vulnerability Tasks, and Enhancements may be available with additional plugins but are not baseline demand artifacts.

questions.stem: As an it_pps_admin, what can you use to detect corrupt data in a project, such as tasks with invalid parents or cyclic relations in a project?
questions.explanation: An it_pps_admin can use Project Diagnostics to detect corrupt data in a project, such as tasks with invalid parents or cyclic relations. Project Diagnostics scans the project structure for data integrity issues and reports problems. System Diagnostics, Edge Encryption Diagnostics, and Analytics Diagnostics are platform tools not specific to project data validation.

questions.stem: In which scenario would using the Copy Project action NOT result in a new project record being created?
questions.explanation: Using the Copy Project action on a new project (one that has not been saved yet) would NOT result in a new project record being created because there is no source project to copy from. Copy Project works on existing projects, sub-projects, and partial projects — but you cannot copy a project that does not yet exist as a saved record.

questions.stem: When copying a source project to a target project, what fields are copied by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: When copying a source project to a target project, the fields copied by default include Duration fields (planned duration), Short description (project name/description), and Planned dates (planned start and end dates). The Number field is auto-generated for the new project and the State is reset to Draft — neither is copied from the source.

questions.stem: The Project management application supports two types of external dependencies. What are they? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Project Management application supports two types of external dependencies: Hard Dependency (strict dependency that prevents task execution until the predecessor completes) and Soft Dependency (advisory dependency that warns but does not block task execution). Milestone, Task, and Change dependencies are not dependency types — they are dependency objects.

questions.stem: In order to map custom fields from Microsoft Project to ServiceNow when importing a project, you must first:

options.text: Export the project to XML format
Create custom fields in your ServiceNow instance

questions.explanation: To map custom fields from Microsoft Project to ServiceNow when importing a project, you must first create custom fields in your ServiceNow instance. The target fields must exist in ServiceNow before the import mapping can reference them. Configuring the form, exporting to XML, and importing the project are subsequent steps.

questions.stem: What is the formula for Committed Utilization?
questions.explanation: The formula for Committed Utilization is Allocated Hours / Capacity. Committed utilization measures the percentage of capacity that has been hard-allocated to work. Forecasted Utilization uses (Allocated + Confirmed) / Capacity. Confirmed Hours / Capacity would be soft allocation utilization, and Assigned Hours is not a standard measure.

questions.stem: How many days is the default sprint length if the length cannot be calculated from the sprint?
questions.explanation: The default sprint length is 14 days if the length cannot be calculated from the sprint. This two-week sprint is the standard default in ServiceNow's agile module. If a sprint record does not have explicit start and end dates that can determine its length, the system defaults to 14 days.

questions.stem: What role is required to view the Details tab of a project in Project Workspace?
questions.explanation: The it_project_workspace_user role is required to view the Details tab of a project in Project Workspace. This role provides read access to project workspace views and tabs. The it_project_manager role is for managing projects, it_project is a base project role, and it_project_user provides basic project access but not specifically the workspace Details tab. The workspace-specific roles (it_project_workspace_*) control access to the Project Workspace interface.

questions.stem: Risks and issues submitted in which forms will be included in the Program record? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Risks and issues submitted in Project, Demand, and Program forms will be included in the Program record. Programs aggregate risks and issues from their associated projects, related demands, and the program itself. Idea and Portfolio forms do not feed risks and issues into program records.

questions.stem: The Program Management application provides the following capabilities to the program manager (Choose three.)

options.text: Create tasks specific to the program.
Create a program by adding related projects and demands
Manage ideas specific to the program

questions.explanation: The Program Management application provides program managers the capabilities to: Create tasks specific to the program (A) for program-level work, Track program costs (B) through cost plans and financial tracking, and Create a program by adding related projects and demands (C). Creating releases for sprints is an agile function, and managing ideas is an ideation function.

questions.stem: Which feature provides a central location for portfolio managers to create and track the roadmap for project and demand execution?
questions.explanation: The Portfolio Workbench provides a central location for portfolio managers to create and track the roadmap for project and demand execution. It displays demands and projects across a timeline, enabling visualization of planned work and resource allocation. Program Workbench manages programs, Project Workspace manages projects, and Demand Workbench evaluates demands.

questions.stem: Why is it recommended to keep the value of the property 'com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration' to 2600 or under?

options.text: Best practices states projects should be no longer than 5 years.
The system is unable to handle more than 2600 tasks.
Because projects longer than 2600 days will no longer load.

questions.explanation: It is recommended to keep the com.snc.project.task.max_task_duration property to 2600 or under to avoid application memory issues. Very long task durations cause the system to generate large numbers of daily allocation records and date calculations that consume excessive memory, potentially causing performance degradation or application errors.

questions.stem: Which role can create a project status report in the Project Workspace?
questions.explanation: The it_project_manager role can create a project status report in the Project Workspace. Project managers are responsible for generating status reports that track project health, progress, and KPIs. The itil, it_demand_manager, and it_project_user roles do not have the ability to create project status reports.

questions.stem: When creating a program, which of the following cannot be part of multiple programs? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When creating a program, a Project and a Demand cannot be part of multiple programs simultaneously. Each project and demand can only belong to one program at a time, ensuring clear ownership and accountability. Tasks and Portfolios do not have this restriction — tasks belong to projects and portfolios contain programs.

questions.stem: Winch role allows you to allocate a resource?
questions.explanation: The resource_manager role allows you to allocate a resource. Resource managers have the authority to review resource plan requests and allocate (hard book) or confirm (soft book) resources to projects. The resource_user, it_project_user, and business_stakeholder roles do not have allocation capabilities.

questions.stem: Why would a program manager create a program? (Choose two.)

options.text: To define the number of sprints

questions.explanation: A program manager creates a program to manage related demands (grouping related business requests together) and to manage related projects (coordinating interdependent project work). Programs provide governance and oversight across multiple related initiatives. Defining sprint numbers is an agile function, and managing portfolios is a portfolio manager function.

questions.stem: Which role in Protect Portfolio Management contains both the resource_user and it_demand manager roles?
questions.explanation: The it_project_manager role in Project Portfolio Management contains both the resource_user and it_demand_manager roles. This combined role allows project managers to both manage resources on their projects and handle demands. Scrum master, itil, and timeline_admin do not contain both of these roles.

questions.stem: In order to allocate an operational resource plan from the Resource Allocation Workbench, which property must be enabled?
questions.explanation: To allocate an operational resource plan from the Resource Allocation Workbench, the property com.snc.resource_management.create_and_manage_operational_resource_plans_from_raw must be enabled. This property enables the creation and management of operational (non-project) resource plans directly from the workbench. The other properties control different resource management features.

questions.stem: The basics of Demand Management include (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The basics of Demand Management include Identify stakeholders (determining who should evaluate and benefit from demands) and Evaluate and qualify tasks (assessing demand viability and quality through the screening process). Creating assessment categories and creating ideas are separate processes from core demand management basics.

questions.stem: At which point in the Demand Management lifecycle do assessments get sent to stakeholders?
questions.explanation: In the Demand Management lifecycle, assessments get sent to stakeholders during the Screening phase. When a demand is submitted and enters screening, the system triggers assessment questionnaires to be sent to registered stakeholders for evaluation. This scoring helps determine whether the demand should be qualified and approved.

questions.stem: When working with demands, which field must be set to “Yes” in order for a user to receive an assessment?
questions.explanation: The Assessment recipient field must be set to 'Yes' for a user to receive an assessment when working with demands. This field on the stakeholder record determines whether the stakeholder will receive assessment questionnaires during the screening phase. Approver, Influence, and Level of Interest capture different stakeholder attributes.

questions.stem: Where is the normalization process used?
questions.explanation: The normalization process is used in Assessment scoring. Assessment normalization adjusts raw assessment scores to a common scale so that demands evaluated by different stakeholders with different scoring tendencies can be fairly compared. This ensures consistent and equitable demand prioritization regardless of assessor bias.

questions.stem: The selections from the Category and Type fields determine the artifact that can be created from a demand. The artifacts can be (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Category and Type field selections determine which artifacts can be created from a demand: Enhancement (minor improvements), Defect (bug fixes, requires Agile 2.0), and Change (change requests). These three artifacts represent the different outcomes of the demand-to-execution conversion. Resources and Tasks are not artifacts created from demands.

questions.stem: In the default system, when working with demands, what two assessment metrics are supported when taking an assessment survey? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In the default system, the two assessment metrics supported when taking an assessment survey for demands are Strategic Alignment (how well the demand aligns with organizational strategy) and Risk (the level of risk associated with the demand). Size and Cost are demand attributes but not default assessment metrics for the survey.

questions.stem: The colors and quadrant labels used in the central location for viewing and assessing business demands?
questions.explanation: The colors and quadrant labels used in the central location for viewing and assessing business demands (the demand workbench) are configured through Workbench Config - Demand. This configuration module lets administrators define the quadrant visualization including colors, labels, and axis definitions. Demand Roadmap, Demand - Config, and System Properties are not the correct locations.

questions.stem: Under the Preferences tab on the Demand form, you have the option to (Choose two.)

options.text: Close a demand on closure of a project
Close a demand on creation of a project

questions.explanation: Under the Preferences tab on the Demand form, you can Close a demand on closure of a project (auto-close the demand when its resulting project closes) and Close a demand on creation of a project (auto-close the demand when a project is created from it). Adding financial benefits and risk scores are done through related lists, not demand preferences.

questions.stem: When a demand is converted to a project, the following fields retain the start and due date (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When a demand is converted to a project, the Approved start date and Approved end date retain the start and due date from the demand. These fields preserve the originally approved timeline from the demand stage. Actual dates are populated as work progresses, not during conversion.

questions.stem: Which roles can add stakeholders to a Portfolio? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The it_pps_admin and it_demand_manager roles can add stakeholders to a Portfolio. These roles have the portfolio management and administration access needed to manage the stakeholder registry. The it_project_user and it_demand_user roles have insufficient privileges for portfolio stakeholder management.

questions.stem: When Agile Development 2.0 and Test Management 2.0 plugins are activated, the project manager can create and edit which of the following phase types depending on execution type? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When Agile Development 2.0 and Test Management 2.0 plugins are activated, the project manager can create and edit Test and Agile phase types depending on execution type. Test phases support test management activities, and Agile phases support agile sprint execution. List and VTB (Visual Task Board) are display types, not phase types.

questions.stem: The combination of the user and the assigned portfolio must be unique when adding a user to which registry?
questions.explanation: The combination of user and assigned portfolio must be unique when adding a user to the Stakeholder Registry. The stakeholder registry ensures each user-portfolio combination is uniquely registered, preventing duplicate stakeholder entries. The UX Page Registry, Event Registry, and Application Registry serve entirely different purposes.

questions.stem: How can the planned start date on a WIP/Closed task be changed?

options.text: By setting the property – 'Enable firing of Business Rules on save from Planning Console'
By setting the property – 'Enable alter of planned date with Actual for Manual Project'
By setting the property – 'Enable altering of planned date(s) for task in WIP/Closed'
By setting the property – 'Enable project cost rollup'

questions.explanation: To change the planned start date on a WIP/Closed task, set the property 'Enable altering of planned date(s) for task in WIP/Closed' to true. By default, planned dates on WIP and Closed tasks are locked. This property unlocks them for modification. The other properties control different aspects of project management.

questions.stem: Project score is calculated based on the individual scores of the following attributes (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Project score is calculated based on Risk Score and Value Score. The project scoring framework evaluates projects by combining risk assessment (potential negative outcomes) and value assessment (expected benefits). Alignment Score and Strategy Score are not separate scoring components in the default project scoring calculation.

questions.stem: The Project Management application enables users to create parent-child relationships between tasks and dependencies, such as finish-to-start and finish-to-finish, between tasks. How many relationships can exist between two tasks?
questions.explanation: Only one relationship can exist between two tasks. The Project Management application allows a single dependency relationship (Finish-to-Start or Finish-to-Finish) between any two specific tasks. Creating a second relationship between the same two tasks is not allowed, ensuring clarity in task dependency chains.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines a parent-child relationship? (Choose two.)

options.text: Parent-child task relationships do not have any effect on task time constraints
A parent-child relationship is not saved as a record in any table
A parent-child task must finish before another begins
Any number of child tasks can be nested under a parent task with or without any dependencies

questions.explanation: Parent-child relationships are defined by: A parent-child relationship is not saved as a record in any table (it is determined by the Parent field on the child task, not a separate relationship record), and Any number of child tasks can be nested under a parent task with or without dependencies. Parent tasks do roll up dates from children, and parent-child is not the same as finish-to-start dependencies.

questions.stem: What can a time card admin or a project manager create to define specific activities in a project?
questions.explanation: A time card admin or project manager can create Subcategories to define specific activities in a project. Subcategories classify time entries into specific work types and activities, enabling detailed tracking of how time is spent. Policies, Time Sheets, and Time Cards serve different purposes in the timecard workflow.

questions.stem: Who can access a project when it is imported into a teamspace from Microsoft Project into ServiceNow?

options.text: A project cannot be imported into a teamspace
Only users who can access the teamspace

questions.explanation: When a project is imported from Microsoft Project into a teamspace, only users who can access the teamspace can access the project. Teamspaces enforce access control — imported projects inherit the teamspace's security boundaries. Projects can be imported into teamspaces, and the access is not open to all users or restricted to only project users.

questions.stem: The overall health of a program rolls up from the latest status report of each project in the program. The status is indicated by which colors? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The overall health of a program is indicated by Yellow (caution/at-risk), Green (on track), and Red (critical/off-track) colors, rolled up from the latest status reports of each project. These are the standard traffic-light health indicators used across ServiceNow PPM. Orange is not a standard program health color.

questions.stem: The PPM Strategic Spend Trading-Generate Strategy/Goal Allocation Breakdowns for Projects and Demands scheduled job is installed, when which of the following is activated?
questions.explanation: The PPM Strategic Spend Tracking scheduled job for generating Strategy/Goal Allocation Breakdowns is installed when Strategic Spend Tracking for PPM is activated. This plugin provides the strategic spend tracking capabilities including the allocation breakdown generation job. Predictive Intelligence, PPM Standard, and Scenario Planning do not install this specific job.

questions.stem: Each teamspace has its own (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Each teamspace has its own Project table and Demand table. Teamspaces provide isolated environments where projects and demands are scoped to the specific teamspace. Resource and Problem tables are shared across teamspaces and are not duplicated per teamspace.

questions.stem: During the allocation process, when named resources are allocated to a plan, where is resource cost derived from?

options.text: Labor rate card for the user
Labor rate card for the fiscal period
Cost specified on the resource allocation

questions.explanation: During the allocation process, when named resources are allocated to a plan, the resource cost is derived from the Labor rate card for the user. The labor rate card defines hourly rates for specific users based on their role, skill level, or other criteria. Cost is not derived from fiscal periods, allocation records, or user records directly.

questions.stem: What is the formula for Forecasted Utilization?
questions.explanation: The formula for Forecasted Utilization is (Allocated Hours + Confirmed Hours) / Capacity. Forecasted utilization includes both hard allocations (committed) and soft allocations (confirmed/tentative) to provide a total picture of expected resource usage. Committed Utilization uses only Allocated/Capacity, excluding soft bookings.

questions.stem: What are the allocation types available on a resource plan? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The allocation types available on a resource plan are Weekly (allocations specified per week), Monthly (allocations specified per month), and Plan Duration (single allocation across the entire plan period). These three types determine the granularity of resource allocation scheduling. Daily and Yearly are not available allocation types.

questions.stem: Resource plan costs are divided into (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Resource plan costs are divided into Planned Cost (estimated cost based on resource requests), Forecast Cost (projected cost considering current allocations and trends), and Actual Cost (actual incurred cost from approved time cards). Allocated Cost and Expense Cost are not standard resource plan cost categories — costs flow through planned, forecast, and actual stages.

questions.stem: On a resource plan, when the attribute for "Derive assignee list from resource plan" is set to true, in what state must the plan be to allow a resource to be added to the assignee field?
questions.explanation: When 'Derive assignee list from resource plan' is true, the resource plan must be in the Allocated state to allow a resource to be added to the assignee field. Only allocated (hard-booked) resources appear in the assignee list. Confirmed (soft-booked), Requested, and Planning states do not make resources available for task assignment under this restriction.

questions.stem: When a user's schedule changes, what action needs to be taken to update their existing data?

options.text: Update calendar manually to reflect the changed capacity

questions.explanation: When a user's schedule changes, you need to update their capacity via 'Update Resource Capacity' action. This recalculates the user's available capacity based on their new schedule. The system does not automatically detect and recalculate capacity when schedules change — the explicit update action must be taken.

questions.stem: If a resource plan is not associated manually to a time card, then a resource plan is auto-associated. The auto-association is done based on which of the following in the time card?
questions.explanation: If a resource plan is not manually associated to a time card, auto-association is done based on the task in the time card. The system matches time card entries to resource plans by looking at the task the time was logged against. If the task belongs to a project with a resource plan for that user, the association is made automatically.

questions.stem: Actuals on a resource plan are updated by what activity?
questions.explanation: Actuals on a resource plan are updated when a time card is approved. The approval of a time card triggers the system to update actual hours and costs on the associated resource plan. Submitting a time card creates the entry but does not update actuals until approval. Project managers do not manually enter actuals, and resource plan approval is a different process.

questions.stem: What must a resource plan contain if a resource plan is associated with a time card?
questions.explanation: A resource plan must contain Hard allocation bookings if it is associated with a time card. Hard allocations (from the Allocate action) create committed bookings that time cards can be charged against. Soft allocations (from Confirm) are tentative and cannot have time cards charged against them. Allocation spread type is unrelated to time card association.

questions.stem: What are the offset types in Benefit Plans?
questions.explanation: The offset types in Benefit Plans are Cost. Benefit plan offset types represent cost deductions or expenses that reduce the net benefit. By specifying cost offsets, portfolio managers can account for expenses that diminish the projected financial return of a project or demand.

questions.stem: Which field, referenced from the cost plan, determines if a cost plan is Capex or Opex?
questions.explanation: The Cost type (resource_type) field, referenced from the cost plan, determines if a cost plan is Capex or Opex. This field classifies the cost plan breakdown as either capital expenditure or operating expenditure. Resource category, Currency type, and Resource plan are different fields that do not determine the Capex/Opex classification.

questions.stem: You can forecast future costs of projects based on (Choose two.)

options.text: Changes in project such as project requirements

questions.explanation: Future project costs can be forecast based on Actual cost incurred (extrapolating from current spending patterns) and Changes in project such as project requirements (adjusting forecasts when scope changes). Incident cost and Paired instances are not factors in project cost forecasting.
